'''Marcin Janusz Gortat''' ({{IPA|pl|ˈmart͡ɕiŋ ˈɡɔrtat}}; born February 17, 1984), also known as "'''the Polish Hammer'''", or "'''the Polish Machine'''", is a Polish former professional [[basketball]] player, and current player development and assistant coach at the [[Washington Wizards]]<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.nbcsports.com/washington/wizards/marcin-gortat-joins-wizards-temporary-assistant-coach | title=Gortat joins Wizards as temporary assistant coach }}</ref> of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). The {{height|ft=6|in=11}}, {{convert|240|lb|kg}} [[Center (basketball)|center]] is the son of [[boxing|boxer]] [[Janusz Gortat]]. He was drafted in the second round by the [[Phoenix Suns]] in the [[2005 NBA draft]] and played for the [[Orlando Magic]], Phoenix Suns, [[Washington Wizards]], and [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. He retired from professional basketball in 2020.

==Early life and career==
As a child, Gortat participated in [[Association football|football]] and [[track and field]], where he competed in the [[high jump]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://basketmania.com.pl/marcin-gortat-najdluzsza-polska-kariera-w-nba_zwdg.a |language=pl |title=Marcin Gortat – najdłuższa polska kariera w NBA |website=basketmania.com.pl |date=5 January 2024 |access-date=30 June 2024}}</ref> His father, [[Janusz Gortat|Janusz]], was a Polish boxer and a bronze medalist in the [[light heavyweight]] class during the [[Munich 1972]] and [[Montreal 1976]] [[Summer Olympic Games|Olympics]], and his mother, [[Alicja Gortat|Alicja]], was a representative of the Poland national team in [[volleyball]]. He has an older brother, [[Robert Gortat|Robert]], who is also a boxer.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://sport.tvp.pl/47519820/marcin-gortat-kto-to-kim-jest-wiek-ile-lat-zona-partnerka-nba-kariera-kluby-reprezentacja-zycie-prywatne |language=pl |title=Marcin Gortat – kto to, kim jest? [kariera, kluby, reprezentacja, życie prywatne] |website=sport.tvp.pl |date=10 April 2020 |access-date=30 June 2024}}</ref>

Gortat grew up in [[Łódź]], Poland, together with his brother [[Filip Gortat|Filip]]. He graduated from [[Technical School]] in Łódź. Apart from Polish, he is fluent in English, German, and Serbian.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://sport.se.pl/pozostale/poligloci-polskiego-sportu-oni-dogadaja-sie-z-kazdym-aa-7Y6f-U4J7-dJXt.html |language=pl |title=Poligloci polskiego sportu. Oni dogadają się z każdym! |website=sport.se.pl |author=Piotr Kożmiński |date=10 October 2014 |access-date=30 June 2024}}</ref> Gortat is also a big [[Motorcycle Speedway]] supporter, often seen supporting Polish club [[Motor Lublin]]. He is also seen regularly at [[Speedway Grand Prix]] events, supporting his good friend, four-time World Champion [[Bartosz Zmarzlik]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://sport.tvp.pl/69856498/nba-marcin-gortat-o-jeremym-sochanie-ciezko-jest-nam-rozmawiac-z-jeremym-jest-on-pierwszoroczniakiem-i-dolacza-do-druzyny-narodowej |language=pl |title=NBA. Marcin Gortat: ciężko jest nam rozmawiać z Jeremym. Jest on pierwszoroczniakiem i dołącza do drużyny narodowej |website=sport.tvp.pl |date=15 May 2023 |access-date=30 June 2024}}</ref>

Gortat started his career with [[ŁKS Łódź (basketball)|ŁKS Łódź]], then played three seasons for [[Köln 99ers|RheinEnergie Cologne]] in [[Germany]]'s [[Basketball Bundesliga]], with whom he won the domestic championship in 2006 as well as the national cup three times.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://impactcee.com/impact/2024/speaker-2/?spk=3325 |title=Meet our speaker - Marcin Gortat |website=impactcee.com |access-date=30 June 2024}}</ref> He also played in the [[2006–07 Euroleague]] season for the first time in the team's history. After being drafted 57th overall in the [[2005 NBA draft]] by the [[Phoenix Suns]] (with his rights later traded to the [[Orlando Magic]]),<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.bulletsforever.com/2016/11/13/13613728/marcin-gortat-players-tribune-column-poland-basketball-youth-system |language=pl |title=Marcin Gortat writes about his NBA journey and the challenges of Polish basketball |website=bulletsforever.com |author=Albert Lee |access-date=30 June 2024}}</ref> Gortat elected to keep playing with Cologne in Germany until 2007.

==NBA career==
===Orlando Magic (2007–2010)===
On August 2, 2007, Gortat signed with the [[Orlando Magic]]. On November 20, he was assigned to the [[Anaheim Arsenal]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Magic Assign Marcin Gortat to NBA D-League|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/Magic_Assign_Marcin_Gortat_to_-244857-66.html|url-status=dead|website=NBA|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091202034620/http://www.nba.com/magic/news/Magic_Assign_Marcin_Gortat_to_-244857-66.html|archive-date=2 December 2009}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Magic Assign Marcin Gortat To Anaheim Arsenal|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/anaheim/gortat_071120.html|url-status=dead|website=NBA|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090318071039/http://www.nba.com/dleague/anaheim/gortat_071120.html|archive-date=March 18, 2009}}</ref> He was recalled from the D-League on December 2,<ref>{{Cite web|title=NBA Development League: 2007-08 Transactions|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/transactions_07-08.html|url-status=dead|website=NBA|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160329075207/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/transactions_07-08.html|archive-date=March 29, 2016}}</ref> and debuted for the Magic on March 1, 2008, against the New York Knicks.

On April 16, 2008, in the Magic's last game of the [[2007–08 NBA season|2007–08 season]], little-used Gortat played 28 minutes<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=280416019 Magic 103, Wizards 83 - box score]</ref> and registered 12 points and 11 rebounds in a 103–83 Magic win over the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=280416019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170319110719/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=280416019|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 19, 2017|title=Magic rest starters, ride Redick, Gortat to blowout of Wizards|website=ESPN|date=April 16, 2008}}</ref> On December 15, 2008, starting in place of the injured [[Dwight Howard]], Gortat played 28 minutes<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=280416019 Magic 109, Warriors 98 - box score]</ref> and recorded 16 points and 13 rebounds in a 108–98 win over the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=281215009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160820030241/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=281215009|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 20, 2016|title=Nelson gets hot in second half to carry Magic past Warriors|website=ESPN|date=December 15, 2008}}</ref> On April 13, 2009, again starting in place of Howard, Gortat played almost 43 minutes and topped his career high in rebounding with 18 rebounds and had 10 points. On April 30, 2009, Gortat made his first playoff start in Game 6 against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], replacing Howard, who was suspended because of his actions in game 5. He had 11 points and 15 rebounds as the Magic eliminated the 76ers 4–2. That Magic playoff run continued all the way to the [[NBA Finals]], making Gortat the first Polish-born player to ever appear in the championship series.

On July 8, 2009, Gortat, a restricted free agent, signed an offer sheet for five years and $34 million with the [[Dallas Mavericks]]. However, Orlando prevented Gortat from going to Dallas by matching the offer sheet on July 13, 2009. Gortat was said to be "very disappointed" to stay with the Magic, since continuing as backup to Dwight Howard would mean limited playing time, whereas playing for Dallas would likely have meant being the starting center.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4324941|title=Magic to retain center Gortat|website=ESPN|date=July 13, 2009}}</ref>

===Phoenix Suns (2010–2013)===
[[File:Al Thornton, Marcin Gortat and Kevin Seraphin.jpg|thumb|Gortat battling for a rebound during his tenure with the Suns]]
On December 18, 2010, Gortat was traded to the [[Phoenix Suns]] along with [[Vince Carter]], [[Mickaël Piétrus]], a 2011 first-round draft pick (which would become [[Nikola Mirotić]]), and $3 million, in exchange for [[Jason Richardson]], [[Earl Clark]], and then-former Magic player and former teammate [[Hedo Türkoğlu]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/suns/news/orlando_trade_101218.html | title=Suns, Magic Complete Six-Player Trade | website=[[NBA]] | date=December 18, 2010}}</ref> Due to [[Steve Nash]] wearing the #13 jersey, which was the number that Gortat had worn in Orlando and Poland, he decided to wear #4 for his tenure with the Suns. During his first season with the Suns, his numbers increased as his minutes grew, initially coming off the bench, then starting at center in place of [[Robin Lopez]]. During his time in Phoenix, Gortat continued to be known as "the Polish Hammer" a nickname originally given to him during his time with the Orlando Magic.

During the [[2011 NBA lockout|lockout-shortened]] [[2011–12 NBA season|2011–12 season]], Gortat averaged 15.4 points and 10.0 rebounds per game. He was the only Suns player to start and play every game of the regular season. Gortat also joined the likes of former Magic teammate [[Dwight Howard]], [[Andrew Bynum]], and [[DeMarcus Cousins]] as the only centers to average a double-double that season. After the season ended, he was named to the [[Polish national basketball team]] for the [[FIBA EuroBasket 2013 qualification]] round. In the second game against [[Finland]], he scored 27 points and grabbed 21 rebounds to help Poland qualify for [[Eurobasket 2013|2013's FIBA Eurobasket tournament]].

On November 7, 2012, he scored 23 points, grabbed 10 rebounds, and had a career-best 7 blocks in a 117–110 victory against the [[Charlotte Bobcats]]. In late February, Gortat suffered a knee injury, and was left off the team for the rest of the season.

===Washington Wizards (2013–2018)===
[[File:Marcin Gortat Wizards.jpg|thumb|Gortat in 2013]]
On October 25, 2013, Gortat was traded, along with [[Shannon Brown]], [[Malcolm Lee (basketball)|Malcolm Lee]], and [[Kendall Marshall]], to the [[Washington Wizards]] in exchange for [[Emeka Okafor]] and a 2014 protected first-round draft pick.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-acquire-gortat-suns|title=Wizards Acquire Gortat From Suns|website=NBA|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=October 25, 2013}}</ref>

On February 27, 2014, Gortat recorded a career-high 31 points and 12 rebounds in a 134–129 triple overtime win over the Toronto Raptors.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Notebook: Wizards 134, Raptors 129 (3OT)|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140227/WASTOR/gameinfo.html|url-status=dead|website=NBA|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140228020518/http://www.nba.com/games/20140227/WASTOR/gameinfo.html|archive-date=February 28, 2014}}</ref> On May 13, he recorded 31 points (his playoff career high) and 16 rebounds to help the Wizards avoid elimination in Game 5 of their second-round series with the Indiana Pacers.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Notebook: Wizards 134, Raptors 129 (3OT)|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140513/WASIND/gameinfo.html|url-status=dead|website=NBA|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140514081542/http://www.nba.com/games/20140513/WASIND/gameinfo.html|archive-date=May 14, 2014}}</ref> He became the first Wizards player with at least 30 points and 15 rebounds in a playoff game since [[Moses Malone]] in 1987.{{Citation needed|date=April 2024}}

On July 10, 2014, Gortat re-signed with the Wizards to a reported five-year, $60 million contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2014/news/07/10/washington-wizards-re-sign-marcin-gortat.ap/index.html|title=Gortat re-signs with Wizards for five years, $60 million|website=NBA|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=July 10, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-re-sign-marcin-gortat|title=Wizards Re-Sign Marcin Gortat|website=NBA|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=July 10, 2014}}</ref>

On December 28, 2015, Gortat was named Eastern Conference Player of the Week for games played December 21–27, earning the honor for the first time in his career.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/2015/news/12/28/players-of-the-week/ Gortat, Westbrook named Players of the Week]</ref> On February 29, 2016, he scored 13 of his 18 points in the fourth quarter and grabbed a career-high 20 rebounds in the Wizards' 116–108 win over the Philadelphia 76ers.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Wall scores 37 as Wizards rally to beat 76ers 116-108|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160229/PHIWAS/gameinfo.html|url-status=dead|date=February 29, 2016|website=NBA|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160301220042/http://www.nba.com/games/20160229/PHIWAS/gameinfo.html|archive-date=March 1, 2016}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Clippers (2018–2019)===
On June 26, 2018, Gortat was traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in exchange for [[Austin Rivers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/news/la-clippers-acquire-marcin-gortat|title=L.A. Clippers Acquire Marcin Gortat|work=NBA.com|date=June 26, 2018|access-date=June 26, 2018}}</ref> On January 5, 2019, Gortat recorded a [[double-double]] with 18 points and 13 rebounds during a 121–111 win over the Suns.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401071249 Clippers beat up on Suns again, win 121-111]</ref> On February 7, he was waived by the Clippers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/la-clippers-waive-marcin-gortat|title=L.A. Clippers Waive Marcin Gortat|website=NBA|date=February 7, 2019}}</ref>

On February 16, 2020, Gortat officially announced his retirement from basketball.<ref>{{cite web|first=Ryan|last=Homler|title=Former Wizard Marcin Gortat announces retirement |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/washington/wizards/former-wizard-marcin-gortat-announces-retirement |website=NBC Sports Washington |access-date=February 20, 2020 |date=February 16, 2020}}</ref>

===Back to Washington Wizards as assistant coach===
In October 2022, he joined the Wizards as temporary assistant coach.<ref>{{Cite news|first=Chase|last=Hughes|title=Gortat joins Wizards as temporary assistant coach|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/washington/wizards/marcin-gortat-joins-wizards-temporary-assistant-coach|url-status=dead|date=October 6, 2022|website=[[NBC Sports]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230321130027/https://www.nbcsports.com/washington/wizards/marcin-gortat-joins-wizards-temporary-assistant-coach|archive-date=March 21, 2023}}</ref>

Gortat brought Polish Heritage Night ({{langx|pl|Polska Noc w NBA}}) back to the [[NBA]] for the first time since retiring. The 9th edition of this event will celebrate Polish heritage when Washington hosts the [[San Antonio Spurs]] with another Pole, [[Jeremy Sochan]] on the roster on March 24, 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|title=NBA: Gortat jest po operacji kolana. Czy wróci do Wizards?|url=https://probasket.pl/nba-gortat-jest-po-operacji-kolana-czy-wroci-do-wizards/|website=Probasket|date=March 17, 2023|language=pl}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Polska Noc w NBA|url=https://bialyorzel24.com/polska-noc-w-nba/|website=bialyorzel24.com|date=March 12, 2023|language=pl}}</ref>

== Controversies ==

=== Incidents with the Washington Wizards ===
In December 2014, Gortat received an official warning from the NBA for violating the league's anti-''flopping'' rules, which prohibit players from simulating or exaggerating contact with an opponent in an attempt to influence an official's decision. The incident occurred on December 14 during a game between the [[Washington Wizards]] and the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite web |date=2014-12-15 |title=Washington's Marcin Gortat Receives Flop Warning |url=https://official.nba.com/washingtons-marcin-gortat-receives-flop-warning/ |access-date=2026-08-28 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On March 18, 2015, again in a game against the Jazz, the league ruled that Gortat had committed a second such violation during the same season. The following day, the NBA fined him $5,000.<ref>{{cite web |date=2015-03-19 |title=Washington Wizards' Marcin Gortat Fined $5,000 |url=https://official.nba.com/washington-wizards-marcin-gortat-fined-5000/ |access-date=2026-08-28 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> Commenting on the matter later, Gortat emphasized the importance of the team's victory and suggested that the result of the game mattered more to him than the fine.<ref>{{cite web |author=Scott Allen |date=2015-03-20 |title=Wizards' Marcin Gortat responds to his critics after flopping fine |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/dc-sports-bog/wp/2015/03/20/wizards-marcin-gortat-responds-to-his-critics-after-flopping-fine/ |access-date=2026-08-28 |website=The Washington Post}}</ref>

In November 2016, following the Wizards' 95–106 loss to the [[Chicago Bulls]], Gortat publicly criticized his team's reserve players, stating that Washington had one of the worst benches in the league. His remarks were criticized because they were made publicly and were seen as potentially contributing to tensions within the team.<ref>{{cite web |author=Candace Buckner |date=2016-11-13 |title=Wizards have a bench problem and it's not getting better |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/wizards/wizards-still-frustrated-by-lack-of-production-from-bench/2016/11/13/4b864a4d-2f7f-4b82-9f00-22541fd55297_story.html |access-date=2026-08-28 |website=The Washington Post}}</ref> Gortat subsequently apologized to his teammates during a team meeting. Head coach [[Scott Brooks]] stressed that the Wizards were one team and should not be divided into starters and reserves.<ref>{{cite web |author=Ava Wallace |date=2016-11-14 |title=Wizards Coach Scott Brooks on Gortat's comments: 'We don't have two teams here' |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/wizards-insider/wp/2016/11/14/wizards-coach-scott-brooks-on-gortats-comments-we-dont-have-two-teams-here/ |access-date=2026-08-28 |website=The Washington Post}}</ref>

In February 2018, a public disagreement arose between Gortat and Wizards leader [[John Wall]]. During Wall's absence due to injury, the team recorded a series of strong results, and after one of the victories Gortat highlighted the team's collective effort on social media. Wall interpreted the comment as a reference to himself and responded publicly. Gortat denied that he had intended to attack his teammate, but the dispute led to a public exchange of comments concerning the atmosphere within the team.<ref>{{cite web |author=Jakub Wojczyński |date=2018-02-07 |title=Medialne spięcie Gortata z liderem drużyny |url=https://przegladsportowy.onet.pl/koszykowka/nba/marcin-gortat-i-john-wall-z-washington-wizards-spieli-sie-w-mediach/79m6n6r |access-date=2026-08-28 |website=Przegląd Sportowy Onet |language=pl}}</ref> A few days later, the two players held a meeting aimed at resolving their differences.<ref>{{cite web |author=Piotr Szarwark |date=2018-02-14 |title=NBA: Gortat i Wall wyjaśnili swoje problemy |url=https://sportowefakty.wp.pl/koszykowka/737723/nba-gortat-i-wall-wyjasnili-swoje-problemy |access-date=2026-08-28 |website=WP SportoweFakty |language=pl}}</ref>

=== TVP ''Wiadomości'' segment concerning the Visa Waiver Program ===
In November 2019, Gortat appeared in a segment of TVP's ''[[Wiadomości]]'' concerning Poland's inclusion in the United States [[Visa Waiver Program]]. The person featured in the report in connection with one of the first flights following the change in regulations was Marcin Bakalarski, who, as media outlets subsequently reported, was a TVP employee and a former activist of [[Law and Justice]]. This led to allegations that the report had been staged in advance. Gortat rejected such suggestions and referred to people accusing him of participating in a "setup" as "idi*ts", which itself became the subject of criticism.<ref>{{cite web |date=2019-11-14 |title="Pierwszy Polak bez wizy" dziennikarzem TVP. W USA witał go Gortat, teraz nazywa krytyków "debilami" |url=https://wiadomosci.gazeta.pl/wiadomosci/7,114883,25408252,pierwszy-polak-bez-wizy-dziennikarzem-tvp-w-usa-wital-go.html |access-date=2026-08-28 |website=Gazeta.pl |language=pl}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=2019-11-14 |title=Dziennikarz TVP i były działacz PiS w "Wiadomościach" jako pierwszy Polak lecący do USA bez wizy. Olechowski: to nie ustawka |url=https://www.wirtualnemedia.pl/wizy-do-usa-zniesione-w-wiadomosci-marcin-bakalarski-jako-pierwszy-polak-lecacy-do-usa-bez-wiz,7170811207264385a |access-date=2026-08-28 |website=Wirtualne Media |language=pl}}</ref>

=== Dispute with Radosław Piesiewicz and the Polish Basketball Association ===
Around the turn of 2019 and 2020, Gortat's public conflict with [[Radosław Piesiewicz]], then-president of the [[Polish Basketball Association]], intensified. Following the Polish national team's strong performance at the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup]], Gortat repeatedly criticized both some of the team's performances and the way Polish basketball was managed. During the Polish Sports Champions Gala in January 2020, Piesiewicz, while accepting an award on behalf of the national team, stated that a leader should be a leader on the court rather than on social media; the remark was interpreted by the media as a reference to Gortat. The former basketball player responded by calling Piesiewicz a "careerist".<ref>{{cite web |author=Karol Wasiek |date=2020-01-05 |title=Plebiscyt na sportowca roku. Zgrzyt na gali. Marcin Gortat mówi wprost: Należy pamiętać o nieobecnych |url=https://sportowefakty.wp.pl/koszykowka/862478/plebiscyt-na-sportowca-roku-zgrzyt-na-gali-marcin-gortat-mowi-wprost-nalezy-pami |access-date=2026-08-28 |website=WP SportoweFakty |language=pl}}</ref>

=== ''WojewódzkiKędzierski'' podcast ===

==== Residents of rural Poland ====
On June 3, 2025, during an appearance on the ''WojewódzkiKędzierski'' podcast following the second round of the [[2025 Polish presidential election]], which was won by [[Karol Nawrocki]], Gortat, who had previously publicly supported [[Rafał Trzaskowski]], criticized the influence of residents of rural areas and smaller towns on the election result.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |date=2025-06-09 |title=Przemysław Czarnek zwrócił się do Marcina Gortata. "Wstyd" |url=https://przegladsportowy.onet.pl/ofsajd/przemyslaw-czarnek-zwrocil-sie-do-marcina-gortata-wstyd/262ve3c |access-date=2026-08-28 |website=Przegląd Sportowy Onet |language=pl}}</ref>

His remarks were criticized as disparaging toward part of the electorate; among those who publicly responded was Law and Justice politician [[Przemysław Czarnek]].<ref name=":0" />

==== Multiplication table and the Baptism of Poland ====
During the same podcast, Gortat was given a series of short questions testing his general knowledge. He was unable to give the date of the [[Baptism of Poland]], identify the author of the Polish novel ''[[Nad Niemnem]]'', or answer a question asking for the result of 7 × 9, which is 63. In response to the last question, he exclaimed "Oh Jesus and Mary", after which host [[Kuba Wojewódzki]] gave him the correct answer.<ref>{{cite web |date=2025-06-09 |title=Marcin Najman uderza w Marcina Gortata. Jaśniej się nie da! |url=https://przegladsportowy.onet.pl/ofsajd/marcin-najman-uderza-w-marcina-gortata-jasniej-sie-nie-da/kh50fkt |access-date=2026-08-28 |website=Przegląd Sportowy Onet |language=pl}}</ref> The excerpt from the interview was subsequently widely discussed in the media, particularly in the context of Gortat's simultaneous involvement in public commentary on social and political issues.<ref>{{cite web |author=Kamil Heppen |date=2025-06-11 |title=Marcin Gortat w ogniu krytyki. Najman uderzył w niego z pełną mocą |url=https://www.se.pl/wiadomosci/po-godzinach/marcin-gortat-w-ogniu-krytyki-najman-uderzyl-w-niego-z-pelna-moca-wielki-mlocie-aa-kT3K-Qmwf-o6gb.html |access-date=2026-08-28 |website=Super Express |language=pl}}</ref>

Among those who publicly commented on the incident was [[Marcin Najman]], who criticized Gortat for speaking out on public issues while at the same time displaying gaps in basic knowledge. In the following months, questions concerning the multiplication table were repeatedly used by his critics as references to the appearance.<ref>{{cite web |title=Marcin Najman wyśmiał Marcina Gortata. Nie uwierzysz, o co go zapytał |url=https://przegladsportowy.onet.pl/ofsajd/marcin-najman-wysmial-marcina-gortata-nie-uwierzysz-o-co-go-zapytal/gwefcfj |access-date=2026-08-28 |website=Przegląd Sportowy Onet |language=pl}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Gortat identifies as a [[Catholic Church|Catholic]] and has said that his faith gives him hope and inspires him.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Świadectwo Marcina Gortata|url=http://www.sport.episkopat.pl/dokumenty/?type=i&id=131|website=sport.episkopat.pl|access-date=20 April 2024|language=pl}}</ref>

In an interview in 2011, Gortat said he preferred his original nickname, "The Polish Machine" to "The Polish Hammer" because when he started out as a pro in Germany a coach told him he "worked like a machine", and a teammate converted that into a nickname.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Marcin Gortat hasn’t always been ‘The Polish Hammer’|first=Scott|last=Allen|date=May 14, 2014|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/dc-sports-bog/wp/2014/05/14/marcin-gortat-hasnt-always-been-the-polish-hammer/|access-date=December 6, 2025|language=en}}</ref> In 2019, he began a relationship with political scientist Żaneta Stanisławska<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-02-03 |title=Żaneta Stanisławska Gortat - wzrost, wiek, mąż - naFakcie.pl |url=https://nafakcie.pl/zaneta-stanislawska-wzrost-wiek-maz/ |access-date=2026-01-18 |language=pl-PL}}</ref>, whom he married in the spring of 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Marcin Gortat potwierdził, że jest już po ślubie! Zdradził szczegóły. "Pobraliśmy się w miarę szybko" |url=https://przegladsportowy.onet.pl/ofsajd/marcin-gortat-po-slubie-potwierdzil-informacje-kim-jest-zona-zaneta-stanislawska/2vn85s9 |access-date=2026-01-18 |website=Przegląd Sportowy Onet |language=pl}}</ref> He is stepfather to his wife's daughter from her previous marriage. In 2026, he had a son, whom he named Marcin Junior.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Marcin Gortat został ojcem! Jest pierwsze zdjęcie syna |url=https://przegladsportowy.onet.pl/ofsajd/marcin-gortat-zostal-ojcem-zaneta-stanislawska-urodzila-jest-pierwsze-zdjecie/7wxx3n9 |access-date=2026-01-18 |website=Przegląd Sportowy Onet |language=pl}}</ref>
